6 Rare & Taboo Anime Horrors You Were Never Supposed to See: Midori, Kakurenbo, Pet Shop of Horrors and More 📼

carousel // Oct 28, 2026

See it on Facebook

How deep does your horror anime archive go? 📼🎃

Before streaming algorithms sanitized anime, the 80s–00s OVA era produced some of the darkest, strangest horror ever animated. Carnival illusions, clockwork soul-hunters, Chinatown blood contracts, cursed Venetian glass, deep-space alien mimics and dark immortality folklore.

Here's the restricted vault, file by file.

The archive: 6 rare & taboo anime horrors

Banned OVAs, cursed folklore and forgotten cult classics that rarely show up on mainstream streaming.

File 01: Midori: Shoujo Tsubaki (1992)

An orphan flower-seller is lured into a grotesque 1920s sideshow, where reality twists into a nightmare. What makes it legendary: Hiroshi Harada animated it almost entirely by himself, painting it by hand over about five years. It's one of the most notorious "you've heard of it but never seen it" anime ever made.

File 02: Kakurenbo: Hide & Seek (2004)

Kids in fox masks are lured into neon ruins to play a forbidden game of hide and seek, and the seekers are demons. A short, independent 3D-animated OVA from YamatoWorks that cult collectors still pass around.

File 03: Pet Shop of Horrors (1999)

Count D sells mythical creatures from his Chinatown pet shop, bound by three ironclad rules. Break one, and you pay with your soul. Studio Madhouse made it as a four-episode series, directed by Toshio Hirata, and it's long out of print.

File 04: Le Portrait de Petit Cossette (2004)

A student working in an antique shop falls for a ghost trapped inside an 18th-century Venetian glass. To free her, he has to suffer for her past. Directed by Akiyuki Shinbo with a Yuki Kajiura score, it's a gothic fever dream.

File 05: Lily C.A.T. (1987)

Twenty light-years from Earth, a sleeper ship wakes up to an alien organism that mimics and liquefies human flesh. It's 80s body horror in space, with designs by the legendary Yoshitaka Amano. If you love Alien, this one's for you.

File 06: Mermaid Forest (1991)

Eat mermaid flesh and live forever, if your body survives the curse without twisting into a monster. Yuta has been wandering for 500 years looking for a cure. It's Rumiko Takahashi's darkest work, from the creator of Inuyasha and Ranma ½, and it gets overshadowed by her lighter hits.

Survived the archive?

Save this vault for your late-night Halloween marathon, and dare to watch one alone at 3 AM.

(Where these are streaming changes by country and over time, so check before you plan your marathon. "Masterpiece" and "hidden gem" are my opinions.)

Sources: Wikipedia: Midori (1992 film)), Wikipedia: Kakurenbo, Wikipedia: Pet Shop of Horrors, Wikipedia: Le Portrait de Petit Cossette, Wikipedia: Lily C.A.T., Wikipedia: Mermaid Saga

Quick answers

What are some rare horror anime from the 80s and 90s? Midori: Shoujo Tsubaki (1992), Lily C.A.T. (1987), Mermaid Forest (1991) and Pet Shop of Horrors (1999), plus 2004's Kakurenbo and Le Portrait de Petit Cossette.

Who made Midori: Shoujo Tsubaki? Hiroshi Harada, who animated it almost entirely by himself over about five years.

Who created Mermaid Forest? Rumiko Takahashi, the creator of Inuyasha and Ranma ½. It's part of her Mermaid Saga.

Who designed Lily C.A.T.? Yoshitaka Amano, the artist known for Final Fantasy and Vampire Hunter D, worked on its designs.
